A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VL-JEPA work, with readable text, equations, figures and tables that can be reliably matched. Both end with references; neither supplied PDF contains a separate appendix.

before.justification: V1 reports original classification, retrieval, VQA, WorldPrediction, controlled training, selective-decoding and ablation results in Section 4.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical evaluations, revises benchmark results and adds action-anticipation experiments in Section 4.4 and Tables 4–5.

M1.justification: The encoder–predictor–decoder architecture, bidirectional InfoNCE objective and selective-decoding procedure remain unchanged. The new forecasting experiments fine-tune the existing model without introducing a documented algorithmic component.

E1.justification: V2 adds future-action anticipation on EPIC-KITCHENS-100 and next-step forecasting on COIN, extending datasets previously used for recognition to different task requirements. Section 3.2 also revises the reported pretraining coverage: PLM-Image-Auto, PLM-Video-Auto and Ego4D are no longer listed, while DataComp, YFCC-100M and Action100M remain.

E2.justification: New Tables 4–5 introduce forecasting comparisons against V-JEPA2 with two vision-encoder configurations, VideoLLM-online, VideoLLM-MoD and ProVideLLM. This substantially extends comparison coverage to JEPA forecasting and streaming-video methods. Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 3.2 replaces 16-frame joint image-video pretraining with 8-frame video training for 60k iterations followed by 32-frame training for 10k iterations. SFT changes from 35k steps with batch size 6k to 83k steps with batch size 3,072. New forecasting protocols report EPIC-KITCHENS-100 Recall@5 at 1, 2, 4 and 10 seconds, plus COIN accuracy. These are reported setting revisions, without establishing which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Table 4 examines sensitivity to the anticipation horizon, showing how forecasting performance and relative advantages vary across four temporal gaps. The existing ablation groups, text hard-negative analysis and selective-decoding frequency study are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-seed variability, confidence intervals or significance tests. Both retain the same average inference-timing procedure using 100 repeated decodings. The signed ablation-table quantities remain performance differences, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces BASE classification/retrieval averages of 46.4/58.4 with 52.5/63.7, and SFT averages of 70.7/59.5 with 75.4/63.8. All four Table 2 VQA scores change; baseline EgoExo4D scores and the ablation table's full-model row also change. New forecasting results include COIN accuracy of 56.2 versus ProVideLLM's 53.6. Training settings differ across versions, so these updates do not isolate a method improvement. WorldPrediction, text-encoder and Figures 3–4 results are retained.

T1.justification: The embedding-space objectives, mathematical mappings and similarity-based selection rules are unchanged. V2 introduces no substantive derivation, formal assumption, theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about embedding prediction, efficiency, selective decoding and unified task coverage. The forecasting extension is reported within the experiments without redefining these headline contributions.

C2.justification: New Section 4.4 interprets forecasting results as evidence that VL-JEPA can handle semantically uncertain prediction tasks. It discusses longer-horizon advantages while acknowledging the larger V-JEPA2 model's stronger one-second result. Existing limitations concerning reasoning, tool use, agentic behavior and scaling remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 3.2 supplies explicit video-pretraining phase lengths and revises training-budget and runtime details, including four rather than two weeks of pretraining on the same 24 nodes of eight H200 GPUs. It adds an Action100M reference for further details. Most architecture and optimizer documentation is retained; forecasting-specific fine-tuning details remain sparse.

R1.justification: V2 adds dataset citations to Table 1, a dedicated Action100M reference, forecasting-baseline references and Terver et al. in the JEPA discussion. The Ego4D reference is removed alongside its removal from the pretraining description. The related-work taxonomy and novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Changes are localized: revised training paragraphs, a new action-anticipation subsection, an experiment roadmap moved before Section 4.1, corrected section references and removal of the unresolved Appendix?? reference. Yejin Bang is added to the author list and acknowledgments are revised. Most prose, including the introduction and conclusion, is retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds forecasting Tables 4–5 and citations within Table 1's column headings. Existing displays are renumbered or relocated, including Figure 4 and the ablation table. The four original figures are preserved without substantive redraws, and the overall layout remains similar.

improvement.justification: The new forecasting experiments provide useful evidence for future-action prediction, and more specific training details and dataset attribution modestly improve documentation. The ablation table's full-model classification/retrieval scores now agree with Table 1. These gains are limited by sparse forecasting fine-tuning details and a new inconsistency: Section 4.1 gives BASE 3.6B training samples, whereas Table 1 gives 3.3B. Higher scores accompany revised training and do not independently establish better methodological evidence.
